## Overview

`oxyc mcp` serves your Oxygen deployment's API to MCP clients over stdio. It
authenticates to the deployment the same way every other `oxyc` command does,
so an assistant can do what that credential can do: read the semantic model,
run queries and automations, and work with custom apps.

<Note>
The older `oxy mcp stdio` and `oxy mcp sse` commands, which served a local
project checkout, have been removed. Use `oxyc mcp` instead.
</Note>

## Install

`oxyc` is Oxy's command-line client (Node 20+):

```bash
npm install -g @oxy-hq/cli
```

## Starting the MCP server

The server's credential is the token in `OXY_TOKEN` and nothing else. With the
variable unset it exits with code `4` before serving a tool, rather than running
on whatever `oxyc login` is cached on the machine. To serve on your own login,
start it with `--login`.

```bash
# an agent, on its own token
claude mcp add oxyc -e OXY_TOKEN=<token> -- npx -y @oxy-hq/cli mcp --env production

# you, on your own login
claude mcp add oxyc -- npx -y @oxy-hq/cli mcp --login --env production
```

Example configuration for Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oxyc": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@oxy-hq/cli", "mcp", "--env", "production"],
      "env": {
        "OXY_TOKEN": "<token>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Tools

Rather than one tool per endpoint, `oxyc mcp` serves four generic tools, so the
tool list stays small and reaches endpoints added after the package shipped:

- `oxy_routes` — search the deployment's API routes
- `oxy_schema` — the request and response schema of a route
- `oxy_request` — call a route
- `oxy_whoami` — who the credential is

Two groups of purpose-built tools sit alongside them, for loops an agent runs
unsupervised: the custom-app sandbox loop (`oxy_env_*`, `oxy_publish_sandbox`,
`oxy_fn_call`, `oxy_checks_run`, `oxy_invocations_*`, `oxy_logs`) and workspace
previews (`oxy_preview_*`). Delete tools need `confirm: true`.

A sandbox agent token (`oxy_sbx_…`) is served a smaller list: the sandbox loop,
`oxy_whoami`, the sandbox secret tools and `oxy_token_revoke`.

The full reference is the `oxyc` README in
[`@oxy-hq/cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@oxy-hq/cli).
